content.text:
I'm mapping out the grid dimensions and identifying the foreground rows and axis row, then tracing the motif's column positions across each row relative to that axis to figure out the wrap edge and coordinate offsets.

I'm testing whether a fixed period like 4, 8, or 11 explains the column patterns for each offset row, checking each candidate against which columns are painted versus not — most small periods fail because they'd predict column 0 as painted when it isn't, so I'm working through period 5, 6, and 7 to see if any produces a consistent match.

Then I realize I mis-set the bounding box — the actual painted range starts at column 1, not 0. Redoing it with columns 1 through 10, period 4 now fits cleanly: the dr=0 row matches columns 2,4,6,8,10 and dr=-1 matches 1,5,9, so I'm checking whether dr=1 similarly lines up with columns following that same mod-4 pattern.

For the lower half, I'm computing mirrored column positions x=21-c and their offsets mod 4 to determine which row (5, 6, or 7) each column lands on, working through all eleven columns to build the reflected pattern.
